issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex omits the /i flag while HAS_KEYWORD includes it, creating undocumented asymmetry
issues.detail: In keyframe-selector-notation, HAS_KEYWORD uses case-insensitive matching but HAS_PERCENTAGE does not. Percentages are digits so case is moot, but the asymmetry signals the data wasn't examined uniformly and risks dropping legitimate uppercase keyword selectors like `FROM`. Normalize both flags or add a comment explaining the divergence.

issues.description: import-notation 'url' branch inverts the gating polarity relative to sibling rules
issues.detail: When primary is 'url', the code returns early if url() IS present — the opposite condition from other rules in this patch. Two reviewers think it's likely correct (skip when already in url form), one suspects a semantic bug. Verify against rule semantics and add a one-line comment documenting the inverted precondition to prevent future 'fixes'.

issues.description: Pre-filter regexes encode an unspecified over-approximation contract vs the parser
issues.detail: Patterns like HAS_NUMERIC `\b(?:100|...|900)\b` and `\burl\(` can match inside comments, var() fallbacks, or attribute selectors. This is safe (only widens to slow path) but the over-approximation invariant is implicit across six rules. The font-weight HAS_NAMED/HAS_NUMERIC case-sensitivity stance is also inconsistent. Document the contract and pick one casing stance.

issues.description: `selectorRegex = /./` sentinel is a clever-instead-of-obvious abstraction leak
issues.detail: Using a match-everything regex to satisfy walkRules' filter signature forces callers to know that `/./` means 'no filter'. Cleaner to branch on whether a filter exists and call `walkRules(cb)` vs `walkRules(filter, cb)`. Same machine code, special case eliminated, clearer intent for the next maintainer.

issues.description: Repeated fast-path pattern across six rules lacks shared abstraction or named contract
issues.detail: Each rule reinvents 'compile a presence regex, bail early if absent.' This is an emerging idiom — name it (e.g. `quickReject`) or add a convention comment so future contributors know the fast-path must over-approximate, not under-approximate. Also tie the regex constants to the same source sets the parser uses so they don't drift.

issues.description: No measurement evidence cited for the performance win
issues.detail: The PR claims a perf benefit but no before/after numbers are recorded on a realistic stylesheet. Adding rough microseconds-per-10k-decls to the changeset or PR body establishes the budget future refactors must protect, and confirms the marginal cases (e.g. selector-pseudo-element-colon-notation's `/:/` filter) actually pay off.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR is a sound, well-shaped performance optimization: cheap presence regexes gate expensive parser walks across six *-notation rules. Two concrete correctness/taste issues recur across all three reviewers — the HAS_PERCENTAGE vs HAS_KEYWORD case-flag asymmetry in keyframe-selector-notation and the inverted gating polarity in the import-notation 'url' branch. The implicit over-approximation contract shared by the six prefilters should be documented, and the `/./` sentinel replaced with a clean filter-or-not branch. Lands after these fixes; no blockers beyond taste and one verification.
